acceptance_criteria: Outbound audit persistence stores no raw chat JID, alias, profile, transport identifier, free-form error text, or reversible message fingerprint.
Every audit outcome uses a closed delivery-truth state machine that distinguishes confirmed sent, confirmed not sent, and ambiguous or reconciliation-required delivery.
A rejected transport promise cannot be recorded as confirmed failure unless the typed transport result proves that no provider-side effect occurred.
Audit read tools expose only authorized, bounded, low-cardinality metadata and cannot filter on or return raw destination identity.
Automatic retention runs through the canonical database-retention owner with explicit windows, protected unresolved states, deterministic counts, and migration-safe indexes.
Migration preserves the minimum evidence needed for idempotency and reconciliation while irreversibly redacting or tombstoning legacy identifying fields.
Reserved synthetic canaries prove identity, alias, profile, transport ID, message-derived hashes, and arbitrary error text are absent from persisted rows and tool results.
Health, documentation, backup, and operator workflows use the same outcome and retention contract.
blast_radius: Every MCP, authenticated health, and Reply Guarantee Protocol send audited through outbound_sends; local database backups and retention; global read_outbound_sends callers; delivery reconciliation and retry decisions; operator investigations; migration compatibility; and any consumer that treats failed as proof that no provider-side effect occurred.

The writer's error sanitizer only truncates to 1,000 characters, and the global read tool returns raw chat identity, profile, transport identifier, and error text. falsifier_or_remaining_gap: The finding would be falsified if the persisted and returned audit projection excluded raw or reversible identity and error material, represented ambiguous delivery separately from confirmed failure, and participated in automatic evidence-aware retention. Exact-main source and focused tests prove the opposite. Product policy must still approve the minimum forensic projection, retention periods, authorization boundary, legacy-row migration, and the shared typed outcome vocabulary coordinated with issue #2559.
impact: A routine audit row can retain and re-expose destination identity, routing aliases, profile names, provider identifiers, message-derived fingerprints, and arbitrary exception text indefinitely. At the same time, a post-provider-call rejection is flattened to failed, which can authorize an unsafe resend even though delivery may have occurred. The result combines privacy exposure, unbounded storage growth, misleading operator evidence, and duplicate-delivery risk.
lead_verification_obligations: Re-read issue #2562, remote main, and every open overlapping pull-request head, body reference, closing reference, and changed-file page immediately before integration.
Coordinate one canonical transport outcome vocabulary with issue #2559 without blocking privacy and retention work that can proceed independently.
Approve the minimum authorized audit projection, identity pseudonymization policy, error taxonomy, retention windows, unresolved-state exemptions, and legacy migration disposition.
Add RED tests with reserved synthetic canaries in destination identity, alias, profile, provider identifier, message text, and thrown error fields.
Prove ambiguous post-provider-call failures never become confirmed not-sent and cannot authorize blind retry.
Prove automatic retention preserves unresolved reconciliation and idempotency evidence while deleting eligible terminal rows transactionally.
Verify migrations are restart-safe, preserve supported legacy rows, and never copy raw legacy fields into a new public projection.
Run outbound audit, send pipeline, MCP audit, database migration, retention, health, Reply Guarantee Protocol, privacy, and documentation guards on committed bytes.

suggested_remediation: Replace the append-forever raw row with a versioned audit projection built from a closed allowlist: opaque non-reversible destination correlation, bounded caller and outcome taxonomy, no free-form error or provider identifier, and explicit confirmed-sent, confirmed-not-sent, ambiguous, and reconciled states. Feed terminal rows into the canonical database-retention sweep while preserving unresolved reconciliation and idempotency evidence. Migrate legacy rows transactionally by redacting or tombstoning unsafe fields, then expose only an authorized bounded read projection.
